module_title: Solar Resource Assessment and Energy Yield

lessons.title: Solar Irradiance Basics and Measurement Units
lessons.body: Solar irradiance is the power of sunlight hitting a surface, measured in watts per square meter (W/mÂ²). When you leave a solar panel in the sun, the irradiance determines how much power it can produce. In Africa, peak sun hours are often 5 to 7 kWh/mÂ² per day, meaning you get the equivalent of 5 to 7 hours of full sunshine. This is called peak sun hours (PSH). For a dam site, you need to know the average daily irradiance to size your pump. A simple tool is a solar pathfinder or a smartphone app like Sun Surveyor. But the most accurate way is to use a pyranometer, which costs around $200-$500. If you can't afford one, you can use satellite data from free sources like NASA POWER or Global Solar Atlas. These give you monthly averages for your exact location. For example, a site in Kenya might have 6.5 PSH in January and 4.5 PSH in July. You need to design for the worst month to ensure water pumping even in cloudy conditions. Remember, irradiance changes with time of day and season. So always use long-term averages, not just one day's reading.

lessons.title: Using Pyranometers and Satellite Data for Dam Sites
lessons.body: A pyranometer measures global horizontal irradiance (GHI). It's a flat sensor that you place level on the ground. For dam sites, you need to measure at the same tilt as your solar panels. A cheaper option is a reference cell, which is a small solar panel that outputs a signal proportional to irradiance. You can buy one for under $100. To use it, connect it to a multimeter and note the short-circuit current. But for most small-scale projects, satellite data is enough. Go to Global Solar Atlas (globalsolaratlas.info) and enter your dam's coordinates. It gives you GHI, direct normal irradiance (DNI), and diffuse irradiance. For pumping, GHI is most important because most pumps use flat panels. If your dam is in a valley, satellite data might overestimate due to shading from hills. So you must do a site visit. Use a compass and a clinometer to measure horizon angles. If a hill blocks the sun before 9 AM or after 3 PM, you lose pumping hours. Also, check for dust and bird droppingsâthey reduce irradiance by 5-10%. Clean panels weekly. For a 1 kW pump, you need about 4-5 kWh/mÂ²/day. In the Sahel, you might get 6 kWh/mÂ²/day, but in coastal Cameroon, only 4.5. Always add a 20% safety margin.

lessons.title: Estimating Solar Energy Potential at the Dam
lessons.body: To estimate energy potential, you need three things: average daily irradiance in peak sun hours (PSH), total solar panel capacity in kilowatts (kW), and system efficiency. The formula is: Energy (kWh/day) = PSH Ã Panel kW Ã Efficiency. Efficiency for a solar pump system is typically 50-60% because of losses in cables, controller, motor, and pump. So if you have 5 PSH and a 1 kW panel, you get 5 Ã 1 Ã 0.55 = 2.75 kWh/day. That energy can pump about 2,750 liters of water to a 10-meter head (assuming pump efficiency of 50%). But you need to know your dam's head and required flow. For example, if you need 10,000 liters per day from a 20-meter deep dam, you need more panels. Use a pump sizing tool like the one from Lorentz or Grundfos. They have free online calculators. Also, consider the tilt angle. In Africa, tilt panels at latitude minus 10 degrees for year-round performance. For a dam in Zimbabwe (latitude 20Â°S), tilt at 10Â° north. This maximizes winter output. If you can't adjust tilt, use a fixed tilt equal to your latitude. Remember, energy yield drops on cloudy days. So design for the worst month. In many parts of Africa, July is cloudy. Use July PSH for design. If July PSH is 4.0, then your daily energy is 4.0 Ã 1 Ã 0.55 = 2.2 kWh. That's your reliable yield.

lessons.title: Seasonal and Daily Irradiance Variations
lessons.body: Solar irradiance changes every hour and every month. In Africa, the dry season usually has clear skies and high irradiance, while the rainy season brings clouds and lower irradiance. For example, in Ghana, March has about 6.0 PSH, but August drops to 4.0 PSH. This means your pump will deliver less water in August. You must plan for this. If your dam is for irrigation, you need water most in the dry season, which is good because that's when irradiance is highest. But for domestic water supply, you need water all year. So size your system for the worst month. Daily variation: from 6 AM to 6 PM, irradiance follows a bell curve. Peak is around noon. A solar pump starts working when irradiance reaches about 200 W/mÂ², which is around 7 AM. It stops when irradiance falls below that, around 5 PM. So you get about 10 hours of pumping, but not at full power. The effective peak sun hours (PSH) is the area under the curve. In practice, you can use a data logger to record irradiance every 10 minutes. If you can't, use the monthly average from NASA POWER. Also, consider the harmattan in West Africaâdust reduces irradiance by up to 30% in December-February. So clean panels daily during that period. For a dam, you can also use a floating solar pump, which benefits from cooling and less dust.

lessons.title: Shading Analysis and Mitigation Strategies
lessons.body: Shading can kill your solar pump's performance. Even a small shadow on one panel can reduce output by 50% or more. At a dam site, common shaders are trees, hills, buildings, and even tall grass. You must do a shading analysis before installing panels. The simplest tool is a Solar Pathfinder, which costs about $300. It has a dome that reflects the horizon, and you overlay a sun path chart for your latitude. You can also use a smartphone app like Sun Surveyor or Solar Shading. Walk around the proposed panel location and note any obstacles. For each obstacle, measure its height and distance. Then calculate the shadow angle: angle = arctan(height/distance). If the angle is greater than the sun's elevation at any time between 9 AM and 3 PM, you have shading. For example, a 10-meter tree 20 meters away gives an angle of 26.6Â°. In winter at noon, the sun might be at 40Â° elevation, so no shading. But in the morning, the sun might be at 20Â°, so shading occurs. To mitigate, cut trees, move panels, or use micro-inverters or power optimizers. For a dam, you can also install panels on a floating platform in the water, which avoids land shading. If shading is unavoidable, oversize the array by 30% to compensate. Also, keep panels clean and free of bird droppingsâthose are small but persistent shaders.

lessons.title: Calculating Daily Energy Yield for Pumping
lessons.body: To calculate daily energy yield, you need the solar array's rated power (W), the average daily peak sun hours (PSH), and the system's overall efficiency. The formula is: Daily energy (Wh) = Array power (W) Ã PSH Ã Efficiency. For a solar pump, efficiency is typically 0.5 to 0.6. So a 1000 W array with 5 PSH and 0.55 efficiency gives 1000 Ã 5 Ã 0.55 = 2750 Wh/day. That's 2.75 kWh. Now, how much water can you pump? Use the formula: Water volume (mÂ³/day) = (Energy (kWh) Ã 367 Ã Pump efficiency) / Total head (m). Pump efficiency is about 0.5 for small pumps. So with 2.75 kWh and 20 m head: (2.75 Ã 367 Ã 0.5) / 20 = 25.2 mÂ³/day. That's 25,200 liters. But you must also consider the flow rate. A pump might be rated at 10 mÂ³/h, but it only runs when irradiance is high enough. So actual daily volume is lower. Use a pump controller with maximum power point tracking (MPPT) to maximize yield. Also, account for cable losses: keep cables short and thick. For a 24V system, use at least 4 mmÂ² cable for runs up to 20 m. If you need more water, add more panels or reduce head. For a dam, you can also use a storage tank to store water during peak sun and use it later. Always monitor your system with a simple energy meter to see actual yield and adjust as needed.

quiz.q: What is the unit of solar irradiance?
quiz.explanation: Irradiance is power per unit area, measured in W/mÂ².

quiz.q: What does 'peak sun hours' (PSH) represent?
options: A) The number of hours the sun shines brightly
B) The equivalent number of hours at 1000 W/mÂ² irradiance
C) The maximum temperature of the sun
D) The time from sunrise to sunset
quiz.explanation: PSH is the total daily irradiance divided by 1000 W/mÂ², giving an equivalent number of hours at peak intensity.

quiz.q: Which tool directly measures solar irradiance?
quiz.explanation: A pyranometer measures global horizontal irradiance.

quiz.q: What is a cheaper alternative to a pyranometer for measuring irradiance?
quiz.explanation: A reference cell is a small solar panel that outputs current proportional to irradiance.

quiz.q: Which free online source provides satellite solar data for any location?
quiz.explanation: Global Solar Atlas provides GHI, DNI, and other solar data for any coordinates.

quiz.q: Why should you design a solar pump system for the worst month?
options: A) To save money on panels
B) To ensure water pumping even in low irradiance conditions
quiz.explanation: Designing for the worst month ensures reliable water supply year-round.

quiz.q: What is the typical efficiency of a solar pump system?
quiz.explanation: Overall system efficiency from solar panel to water output is typically 50-60%.

quiz.q: What formula calculates daily energy yield from a solar array?
options: A) Energy = PSH Ã Array power Ã Efficiency
quiz.explanation: Daily energy (Wh) = PSH Ã Array power (W) Ã System efficiency.

quiz.q: In Africa, what tilt angle is recommended for fixed solar panels?
quiz.explanation: Tilting panels at latitude angle maximizes year-round solar capture.

quiz.q: What is the effect of dust on solar panels?
quiz.explanation: Dust blocks sunlight, reducing irradiance and energy yield by 5-10% or more.

quiz.q: Which season typically has lower solar irradiance in West Africa?
quiz.explanation: Rainy season brings clouds that reduce irradiance.

quiz.q: What is the approximate time a solar pump starts working in the morning?
quiz.explanation: Pumps start when irradiance reaches about 200 W/mÂ², around 7 AM.

quiz.q: What is the harmattan and how does it affect solar panels?
options: A) A dry dusty wind that reduces irradiance
B) A rainstorm that cleans panels
quiz.explanation: Harmattan dust reduces irradiance by up to 30%, requiring frequent cleaning.

quiz.q: What is a common shading analysis tool?
quiz.explanation: Solar Pathfinder is a simple tool to assess shading at a site.

quiz.q: How can you mitigate shading from a tree?
quiz.explanation: All these methods can reduce or eliminate shading effects.

quiz.q: What is the formula for water volume pumped per day?
options: A) Volume = Energy Ã 367 Ã Pump efficiency / Head
quiz.explanation: The formula relates energy, pump efficiency, and head to water volume.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of an MPPT controller?
options: A) To maximize power output from panels
quiz.explanation: MPPT (Maximum Power Point Tracking) optimizes panel output under varying conditions.

quiz.q: Why is cable size important in a solar pump system?
options: A) To reduce voltage drop and power loss
quiz.explanation: Thicker cables reduce resistive losses, improving system efficiency.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of floating solar panels on a dam?
options: A) Reduced shading from land obstacles
quiz.explanation: Floating panels avoid land shading and benefit from cooling.

quiz.q: What does GHI stand for?
quiz.explanation: GHI is the total solar irradiance on a horizontal surface.

quiz.q: Which of these is a free satellite data source for solar irradiance?
quiz.explanation: NASA POWER provides solar and meteorological data for any location.

quiz.q: What is the typical daily energy yield for a 1 kW array with 5 PSH and 55% efficiency?
quiz.explanation: 1 kW Ã 5 PSH Ã 0.55 = 2.75 kWh.

quiz.q: Why is it important to clean solar panels regularly?
options: A) To maintain irradiance and energy yield
B) To make them look nice
quiz.explanation: Dust and dirt block sunlight, reducing output.

quiz.q: What is the effect of a 20% safety margin in system sizing?
options: A) It ensures reliable water supply even in worse conditions
quiz.explanation: A safety margin accounts for uncertainties and degradation.

quiz.q: What is the approximate efficiency of a small solar pump?
quiz.explanation: Small pumps typically have about 50% efficiency.

quiz.q: What is the best tilt angle for a dam site in Zimbabwe (latitude 20Â°S)?
quiz.explanation: Tilt at latitude minus 10 degrees facing north for year-round performance.

quiz.q: How does shading on one panel affect the whole array?
options: A) It can reduce output by 50% or more
D) It only affects that panel
quiz.explanation: Shading one panel can disproportionately reduce the entire array's output.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a storage tank in a solar pump system?
options: A) To store water for use during low irradiance
quiz.explanation: Storage tanks allow water to be used when the sun isn't shining.

quiz.q: What is the typical daily pumping duration for a solar pump in Africa?
quiz.explanation: Solar pumps operate about 10 hours per day, from 7 AM to 5 PM.

quiz.q: What is the formula to calculate shadow angle?
quiz.explanation: The shadow angle is the arctangent of height divided by distance.
